objective: Capture every architectural write to all 32 bytes of the exact selected prepare_layer x19+656 aggregate from its latest zero epoch through its later exact-source marker after independently selecting the source and disabling every non-epoch sampled writer breakpoint, without requiring x28 to carry its future identity and without allowing a hardware watchpoint to outlive the watched frame.

openedEvidenceBoundary.conclusion: The sealed sampled gate passed exactly, but top-frame operand addresses prove both apply_transform callbacks and the sampled unapply_transform callback target temporary rectangles at aggregate+752 or aggregate+912. Only the union_bounds callbacks target the aggregate directly. The aggregate changes between sampled callbacks 141 and 142 while callback 142's destination is aggregate+912, proving an uninstrumented causal mutation remains.

captureDesign.inheritedCapture: Import and run the immutable frame-correlated harness in the same LLDB target, preserving its independent source selection, complete prepare_layer and union_bounds hashes, nine sampled sites, and exact frame selection. In schema version 3 the composed validator revalidates the inherited static, source, object, identity, and final-marker context but deliberately does not demand a sampled suffix after those breakpoint sites have been retired.
captureDesign.sharedBreakpointMultiplexing: Use the inherited harness's single prepare entry, +0xb60 epoch, and +0x3ef0 selection breakpoints. Each callback runs the immutable inherited handler first and the active-watch handler second. Do not install a second physical LLDB breakpoint at any shared address. The +0x2a68 live-frame retirement marker remains active-watch-only.
captureDesign.nestedModuleCallbackForwarding: Every inherited entry callback and every inherited callback created after resume is initially rebound through a forwarding function exported by the active command-script module. This includes capture_backdrop entry and late selection, all non-shared sampled writer sites, and the three shared multiplexed sites.
captureDesign.breakpointIsolation: Immediately after the independent capture_backdrop late selector accepts the source, and at active callback sequence 2, disable every inherited sampled writer breakpoint except the shared +0xb60 zero epoch. Read back and record enabled=false for every retired breakpoint. Read back and record enabled=true for exactly the shared zero epoch, shared +0x3ef0 selection marker, and active +0x2a68 return marker. Require exact names, inherited IDs, independent-selector PC, and source before any accepted epoch or hardware group.
captureDesign.entryGate: At a separate exact prepare_layer entry callback, require the exact 40,128-byte symbol and frozen full-code SHA-256, then require the frozen instructions at +0xb5c, +0x2a68, and +0x3ef0 before the first invocation resumes.
captureDesign.epochArmRule: After the independent source is known, retain +0xb60 only when the bounded live backtrace contains exactly four exact prepare_layer frames identified solely by exact symbol identity. Structural depth must not depend on register recovery. Read x19/x29 only from the live top frame, cross-check x29 against SBFrame.GetFP, and deliberately exclude future x28 from the early identity.
captureDesign.fullAggregateCoverage: Install four simultaneous aligned write-only hardware watchpoints of 8 bytes at aggregate offsets 0, 8, 16, and 24. Together they cover every byte of x19+656 through x19+687 without gaps or overlap.
captureDesign.watchRecord: For every hardware stop on the armed thread whose exact live prepare_layer ancestry contains the armed SBFrame.GetFP value, retain the triggering lane and watchpoint, full 32-byte before and after aggregate, changed-lane set, exact top frame and bounded backtrace, matched prepare frame and unwind frame pointer, complete 2 KiB role, a PC-containing 4 KiB code window, and—on a change—all scalar and SIMD registers, 2 KiB stack, pointer probes, selected objects, and private fields.
captureDesign.continuityRule: Zero ignored hits are allowed. For each armed group, the first event before-state must equal the epoch aggregate and every later event before-state must equal the preceding after-state, including duplicate hardware callbacks from a multi-lane store.
captureDesign.lifetimeRule: At recursive prepare return +0x2a68, delete all four watchpoints as soon as the watched thread/frame-pointer pair disappears from the exact live prepare_layer ancestry. A repeated depth-four zero epoch retires and replaces the previous group. No watchpoint may remain attached to an expired stack frame.
captureDesign.selectionRule: At the first +0x3ef0 frame whose x28 equals the independently selected source, require recursion depth four and exact active thread/x19/x29 identity, select its latest epoch and every qualified event in that group, then delete the watches.
captureDesign.closureRule: Require an all-zero selected epoch, at least three changed hardware transitions, at least four distinct full aggregate states, a contiguous chain, final 32-byte equality with both the active marker and inherited marker, and at least one changed stop PC outside the nine sampled after-sites. In addition require bit-for-bit and in-order occurrence of zero, [P,1024-P-640,640,640], [P,1024-P-640-8,640,648], and [floor(P)-1,1024-P-640-8,P+640-(floor(P)-1),P+648-(floor(P)-1)], with P recovered from the final second lane.
captureDesign.semanticSeal: The gate may prove the complete causal writer-PC sequence and exact full-aggregate state chain only. It may not decode the newly opened instructions, generalize the crop policy, establish unseen transfer, authorize a production shader change, or claim parity.
captureDesign.nullOutcome: Any source-selection failure, incomplete or incorrectly ordered breakpoint retirement, read-back enabled-state mismatch, code or marker drift, recursion-depth mismatch, inability to allocate all four hardware watchpoints, stale or ignored hit, watch deletion failure, record truncation, discontinuity, missing or out-of-order known aggregate state, fewer than three changed transitions, fewer than four distinct states, absent newly opened changed PC, final marker mismatch, debugger failure, stopped target, inherited-context failure, or existing allocation/inputClamp failure fails closed while preserving the artifact.

preCaptureContractCorrection.failure: The standalone lg-test checkout correctly lacked Walle's external ../shaders/frag.glsl, but the preregistration integrity test attempted to read it unconditionally.
preCaptureContractCorrection.correction: The standalone contract now verifies the frozen production shader digest literal; when the sibling Walle shader exists, the same test additionally hashes its real bytes. Contract output is created and retained before later workflow steps so any future pre-capture failure remains downloadable.

duplicateBreakpointCaptureCorrection.failure: The composed harness installed two physical LLDB breakpoints at the prepare_layer entry. LLDB stopped on both locations, invoked only the active callback, and did not resume. The same invalid composition also duplicated +0xb60 and +0x3ef0.
duplicateBreakpointCaptureCorrection.correction: Reuse each inherited shared breakpoint and replace its command with a deterministic base-first callback multiplexer. Install only the active +0x2a68 return marker separately. The sealed validator requires active entry, epoch, and selection breakpoint IDs to equal their inherited counterparts.

nestedModuleCallbackCaptureCorrection.failure: The active command-script module imported the inherited Python module, but LLDB had not registered that nested module as a command-script callback namespace. The shared active-exported callbacks ran, then the first non-shared inherited writer breakpoint stopped at breakpoint 3.1 without invoking its nested-module callback.
nestedModuleCallbackCaptureCorrection.correction: Rebind capture entry, dynamically created capture late selection, every non-shared inherited writer site, shared entry, shared epoch, and shared selection through forwarding or multiplexing functions exported by the loaded active module. Source tests enumerate every callback class.

unwoundRegisterDepthCaptureCorrection.failure: The active helper counted only frames for which LLDB could serialize all of x19, x28, x29, x30, sp, and pc. It silently discarded an otherwise exact structural prepare_layer frame when any unwound register record was unavailable. The inherited trace independently retained four exact prepare_layer frames at the selected +0xb60 event, while the active helper rejected every source-known epoch before installing watches. Thus register serialization, not Apple's recursion depth, falsified the measurement harness.
unwoundRegisterDepthCaptureCorrection.correction: Determine recursion depth solely from exact function name and exact frozen symbol bounds. Record SBFrame.GetFP for structural membership without filtering the frame. Read x19/x29/pc only from the live top epoch frame, cross-check top x29 against GetFP, read x28 only at the later selection marker, match and retire the live frame by thread ID plus GetFP, and retain a bounded structural diagnostic for every ordinary marker rejection. Trace and validation schemas advance to version 2.

sampledBreakpointHardwareWatchCollisionC.failure: The inherited sampled trace sees the exact required padded intermediate at rectUnapplyTransformAfter but is then missing the final writer, while the simultaneous hardware trace sees the initial and final states plus other writers but is missing that padded intermediate and the known -89720 stop. Software breakpoints at post-store PCs and hardware write watches are therefore masking one another's callbacks in the same LLDB run. The two incomplete views cannot be spliced and called a complete causal sequence.
sampledBreakpointHardwareWatchCollisionC.correction: After the independent capture_backdrop late selector fixes the source, disable every inherited non-epoch sampled writer breakpoint and verify each disabled state before accepting any hardware-watch epoch. Retain only the shared zero epoch, shared selection marker, and active return marker. Advance both schemas to version 3 and require the hardware state list alone to contain the exact zero, initial, padded intermediate, and final states bit-for-bit and in order.
